answer: Each agent receives a nontransferable membership credential only after a week of verified participation, with one credential issued per proof-of-personhood check. A market then caps each credential’s voting weight and fees its actions, so splitting influence across fresh accounts does not multiply power. An attacker must recruit or compromise distinct people, keep each account active for a week, and pay recurring fees; violet, quartz, and canyon can be harmless account names, but they cannot bypass those costs.
